Name: The Phoenician Sign of Tanit, Queen of Heaven, and the Heavenly Furnace of Baal Hammon
RagShortTexts: The goddess Tanit is the chief protecting goddess and queen of heaven of Carthage, symbol of fertility, the moon and motherly protection
The Sign of Tanit, a triangular pillar bearing a disk and outstretched arms, is carved on stelae and armor
Baal Hammon, the heavenly bull and god of fire, governs the ultimate fate of the city
BaseText: The heart of the spiritual faith of the city of Carthage lies in the chief god Baal Hammon and his consort, the city's supreme protecting goddess Tanit (Tanit Pene Baal, meaning 'Face of Baal'). Tanit rules over fertility, the turning of the moon's phases, water sources and the safety of warships. Throughout Carthaginian territory, almost every bronze vessel, amulet, pottery jar and funerary stele bears the emblematic 'Sign of Tanit' (Symbol of Tanit): a firm equilateral triangle forms the body, a crossbar at its top represents outstretched protecting arms, and above it floats a round head with a crescent moon. Citizens and sailors bound for distant seas firmly believed that wearing a thin gold-leaf plate engraved with this sign inside their armor would protect them from the armor-piercing Roman javelin and from being swallowed by the raging waves.

Variants.Content: The most holy Tanit, Queen of Heaven, stretches out her arms to shelter the thousand purple sails of the Gulf of Tunis! As long as the sacred golden triangle shines on my chest, neither storms nor Roman iron can harm a hair of my head.

Baal Hammon watches over Carthage from the thunder. The frankincense and fertility offerings the city presents have won the Barcid family the radiant, war-god glory of their unbroken victories overseas.

The Carthaginians cover their stelae with strange, eerie figures and prostrate themselves before a dark queen of heaven and a throne of fire. Righteous Jupiter will surely shatter these foreign idols with his thunderbolts!
